content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT fired 1799004321 - gpu-node-az2-14 - ECC_ERROR_RATE > 2/m for 10m. Pager: @sam. See: https://internal.redwood/alerts/1799004321

sam: paging — oncall getting this now. will triage.

maya: i'm oncall too, standing by. quick summary?

sam: initial find: ECC error spikes on az2-14, multiple GPUs showing corrected ECC counts increasing. A subset of serving pods experienced OOM-ish failures, fallback to smaller model variant for some requests. Customers: two medium customers saw transient 5xx and higher tail latency (~95th 1200ms) for ~8m.

jin: pulling telemetry...

jin: prom query:```
rate(gpu_ecc_corrected_total{node="gpu-node-az2-14"}[5m]) > 2
```

jin: also seeing VRAM pressure on that node:```
gpu_memory_used_bytes{node="gpu-node-az2-14"} / gpu_memory_total_bytes{node="gpu-node-az2-14"} > 0.9
```

kevin: thermal sensor logs look noisy but not above critical: `gpu_temp_celsius{node="gpu-node-az2-14"} ~ 85-88C` — high but within sustained turbo for this hw. ECC is the weird one.

ellie: support report incoming, two customers flagged errors; they're being routed to canary model fallback so no data loss reported. customers want ETA.

sam: mitigation plan: 1) cordon + drain node to stop new pods landing 2) force pod migrations off node 3) reduce batch size for serving pods globally for 10m to reduce memory pressure 4) mute noisy ECC alerts for this node during remediation to avoid paging noise.

maya: agree. i can do the drain and live-remediate. jin can watch telemetry. kevin can prepare kernel/driver rollback if needed. ellie pls patch customers.

sam: executing drain:```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-az2-14
kubectl drain gpu-node-az2-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

ops-bot: Command accepted. Drain started at 1799004560. 6 pods evicted.

jin: seeing pod migrations begin. VRAM pressure dropping on the node. ECC rate still elevated but trending down.

sam: temporarily muting ECC alert rule for node gpu-node-az2-14 (10m window) to avoid repeated pages. muting rule id mute-az2-14-1799.

incident-bot: Silence applied: mute-az2-14-1799 until 1799005160.

kevin: logging driver/firmware check. nothing obvious in dmesg other than corrected ECC counts. going to collect nvml dump.

jin: also lowering batch size via rollout to serving config (canary to 10% then 100%):```
PATCH /api/v1/configs/serve-batch
{"max_batch_size": 8}
```

ops-bot: Config rollout started, canary 10% at 1799004800.

ellie: customer msg sent: "We're aware of transient errors and latencies for a subset of requests; mitigation in progress, expect stability within 15-30 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause." :white_check_mark:

sam: after drain, node still shows corrected ECC events but lower. currently no 5xx reports. testing at scale for 10m.

maya: agree keep monitoring 30m. if ECC persists => consider offlining GPU board and swapping or rebooting host.

jin: creating a short dashboard to track these metrics across the cluster (ECC rate, gpu_memory_ratio, gpu_temp, pod_restarts). Link to temp dash: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/temp/gpu-incident-1799

kevin: quick post-incident configs we should do: 1) increase ECC error alert threshold from 2/m to 5/m for single-node to reduce noise (but keep cluster-wide rule for patterns) 2) add VRAM pressure rule firing at 95% for 3m instead of 1m 3) add a dashboard panel to correlate ECC bursts with VRAM pressure and pod eviction rate.

sam: agreed. but want careful: raising ECC threshold could hide real hardware failures. propose: change to 5/m for node-level alert but add a new alert that looks for ECC bursts across >=2 nodes within 10m to keep global sensitivity.

kevin: i'll open INF-4721 to track alert rule changes. tentative rules in the ticket:```
- alert: GPUNodeECCBurst
  expr: increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[10m]) >= 5
  for: 2m
  labels: {severity: warning}
- alert: GPUClusterECCPattern
  expr: sum(increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[10m])) by (cluster) >= 10
  for: 1m
  labels: {severity: critical}
```

maya: also create runbook steps for oncall for ECC bursts: quick checks, when to drain vs when to schedule host swap. I'll add to runbooks under runbooks/gpu-ecc.md.

ellie: follow-up: customer postmortem emails queued once we confirm root cause.

ops-bot: Drain finished at 1799004988. Node cordoned: true. No new pods scheduled.

jin: telemetry stable. VRAM ratios back to normal on cluster. ECC events returned to baseline.

sam: closing active pager. moving to post-incident channel for writeup. highlights: cause likely transient memory soft-errors correlated with high batch memory pressure; mitigated by draining node + batch size reduction; no data loss; customers rerouted temporarily.

maya: assigning follow-ups: INF-4721 (alert tuning) -> kevin, DASH-83 (permanent GPU incident dashboard) -> jin, RUNBOOK-19 (ECC runbook) -> maya. ETA: 1 week for alerts/dash, 2 weeks for runbook and hardware follow-up.

kevin: noted. will include automated test for the new alert logic in CI.

sam: thumbs. thanks team. I'll create postmortem skeleton and paste logs.

incident-bot: Pager resolved at 1799005120 by sam.

ops-bot: Handoff: oncall -> nextshift at 1799005200.

maya: i'm nextshift, i'll pick up any leftover items tomorrow morning.

sam: thanks all. closing thread and adding to incidents folder. :slightly_smiling_face:
